$comment: THE ONE FILE YOU EDIT. Everything about your business lives here.
Nothing about your business is written into the app's code.
You should not have to touch this by hand. Open the project in Claude and
say 'install this' — it asks you a few questions and fills this in for you.
Run `npm run doctor` after any change. It checks this file against your
settings and tells you exactly what is still missing.
NEVER put passwords or tokens in here. This file is safe to share. Secrets
live in .env.local on your computer, or in your hosting settings online.
`name` is just what shows at the top of the dashboard.
`timezone` is the timezone your META AD ACCOUNT reports in — not where
you live. Find it in Ads Manager under Billing. Get this wrong and your
days are cut in the wrong place, so 'yesterday' means the wrong thing.
`currency` is the currency Meta CHARGES YOU in. It is used for ad spend
only. Your sales figures are read exactly as you wrote them and are
never converted.
`salesCalendarIds` are the calendars in your booking tool that hold
SALES calls. Not onboarding calls. Not coaching calls. Leave it empty
at first, then run `npm run calendars` once a few bookings have come in
and it will show you the real ids to paste here.
business.name: My Coaching Business

$comment: Your sales tracker. Turn this off and the dashboard still works — you get
spend, DMs, booked calls and show rate. You do NOT get revenue, and
without revenue there is no ROAS. So you almost certainly want this on.
TWO WAYS TO CONNECT IT, and the app works out which you used:
1. PUBLISHED LINK (easier, no Google Cloud account needed)
In your sheet: File > Share > Publish to web > pick the tab >
Comma-separated values (.csv) > Publish. Paste that link into
SHEET_URL in your settings. It stays live: edit the sheet and the
dashboard sees it on the next update.
2. API KEY (use if you would rather not publish anything)
Set GOOGLE_SHEETS_API_KEY and GOOGLE_SHEETS_SPREADSHEET_ID instead.
`tabs`: 'monthly' means one tab per month, named like `monthTabFormat`.
'single' means one tab that everything goes in, named by `tab`.
A published link always points at ONE tab, so it implies 'single'.
`columns` maps YOUR sheet's letters onto what the dashboard needs. Only
`date` and `prospectName` are required. Anything you leave out simply
shows no data rather than a wrong guess.
`manychatLink` is worth more than all the other optional columns put
together. It is a column where whoever takes the call pastes the
ManyChat chat link. That link is what ties a sale back to the DM, and
therefore back to the ad that caused it.
THE NAMING RULE. The keyword is the LAST WORD of the ad's name. The name
is split on | : ( ) [ ] { } _ - and the last word of the last piece wins:
"Test | Direct CTA | TRIM"   -> trim
"Q3 Scaling (PRIMED)"        -> primed
"Lead Magnet | 50 | Tempo"   -> tempo
This is the whole connection between money you spent and DMs you got.
Name an ad without its keyword at the end and the spend still records,
but it can never be credited with a DM, a call, or a sale.
`factsLookbackDays` is how far back every update rebuilds. It needs to
comfortably beat your longest view (30 days) plus how long people take
to buy after they first message you.
